question: Even in 1990, what proportion of the country’s population continued to be employed in agriculture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**65%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1990, approximately **65% of India's population** was employed in agriculture.
 
• Agriculture has historically been the backbone of the Indian economy, providing livelihood to a significant portion of the population.
 
• The high proportion of agricultural employment reflects the rural-based demographic and economic structure of the country during that period.
 
• This trend has gradually declined over the years due to urbanization, industrialization, and shifts towards the service sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution**

 
 
• The Green Revolution began in the 1960s and introduced high-yielding variety seeds and modern agricultural techniques to India.
 
• It significantly increased food grain production, particularly in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• This movement helped India transition from a food-deficient to a food-surplus country.
 
 
 
• **Rural Employment Schemes**
 
 
• The government has launched several schemes to boost rural employment, such as the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).
 
• MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage employment to rural households to enhance livelihood security.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Reforms**
 
 
• Recent reforms aim to liberalize agricultural markets, improve infrastructure, and boost farmers' income.
 
• However, these reforms have faced significant opposition from various farmer groups.
 
 
 
• **Economic Transition**
 
 
• India has experienced a shift from an agriculture-based economy to one dominated by services and manufacturing.
 
• Despite this shift, agriculture still employs a substantial portion of the rural population.
